name: Papadmalji Agro Foods
lm_rationale: Kreo Capital Pvt.Ltd. — no 2026 record on chittorgarh's SME tracker; RHP past-issue table lists 3 listed SME IPOs (3C IT Solutions -17.29%, Active Infrastructures 0.00%, Shree Kanha Stainless -2.22% open vs issue price), 0 of 3 positive, -6.50% avg listing-day open; all three were down 6-70% by day 30.
net_proceeds: ₹7.90 Cr for a new 45,000 sq ft rice-papad/machine-made unit at Bachhasar, Bikaner (₹4.41 Cr building, ₹2.81 Cr machinery, ₹0.68 Cr 250 kW rooftop solar) and ₹5.80 Cr to repay bank borrowings; the rest is general corporate purposes. The ₹1.66 Cr OFS goes to India Customer Insight Fund, not the company.
key_risks: Working capital is heavy, with inventory of ₹24.99 Cr against FY26 revenue of ₹33.53 Cr, and the top 10 customers made up 45.94% of FY26 revenue. There is also a ₹2.77 Cr income-tax reassessment demand under appeal.
market_moat: Its own brands (Zhakaas, Vishal, Rozana, Diamond, Papadmalji) are sold in 21 states and 3 UTs through general trade, modern trade, quick commerce and D2C. Hand-made papads come from a women-led Batara-Batari home-rolling network in Bikaner.
management: Promoters Jai Agarwal, Prem Lata Agarwal and Aanya Agarwal; 60.98% pre-issue promoter holding drops to 44.28% post-issue.
prose_business: Papadmalji makes hand-made, machine-made and rice (khichiya) papads, vrat papads and moongodi at two FSSAI-licensed units in Bikaner. It also does white-label hand-made papad manufacturing and trades cereal pellets. FY26 revenue from operations was ₹33.53 Cr.
highlight_dev: A new ₹7.90 Cr Bachhasar, Bikaner unit will take over rice-papad (khichiya) production, where FY26 utilisation was 93.15%, and add 5"/7" rice papads and mini machine-made papads. The rented Karni unit then closes.
sector_outlook: The RHP's industry section puts India's food processing market at Rs. 33,052.5 billion in FY25 and expects Rs. 65,835 billion by FY34. It also describes papad as a fragmented, price-sensitive segment dominated by unorganised players.
gov_scheme: The company says it is eligible for a capital subsidy under the Rajasthan Investment Promotion Scheme, 2024 (RIPS 2024): 50% of capital investment, capped at ₹1.50 crore and paid at 5% a year for 10 years. Sanction and timing are not assured.
peer_sentence: The RHP has no peer comparison. It says no listed company in India is exclusively in papad manufacturing or of comparable size, so the 12.97x post-issue P/E cannot be benchmarked against a document peer set.
verdict_reason: 12.97x post-issue P/E is reasonable, but FY26 revenue grew only 5.59%, inventory is heavy and the LM record is negative
why: FY26 total income rose 5.59% to ₹33.54 Cr and PAT 10.33% to ₹5.21 Cr. PBT grew 53.46% (₹4.72 Cr to ₹7.24 Cr), but FY25 carried no current tax, which flattens reported PAT growth. At ₹72 the issue is priced at 12.97x FY26 EPS on post-issue shares and 3.04x NAV, with D/E of 0.62. About 58% of the itemised proceeds fund a new Bikaner unit and the rest repays bank debt. Kreo Capital's three prior SME listings opened flat-to-negative on average (-6.50%). Promoters fall to 44.28% post-issue. The main risk is working capital: FY26 inventory was ₹24.99 Cr.
suggestion: Watch: apply only for the long term if subscription is strong. The lead manager's record and minority promoter stake make listing gains uncertain.
documents: drhp-cache/papadmalji-agro-foods-rhp.pdf (RHP dated 23 Sep 2026, 461 pages; source papadmalji.com link from chittorgarh)
discrepancies: No chittorgarh figure conflicts with the RHP. Financials, KPIs, EPS, NAV and promoter % all match. chittorgarh's P/E 9.42/12.97 uses FY26 EPS on pre-issue and post-issue shares, so it is correct.
The RHP leaves issue amounts as [●]. The ₹18.52 Cr fresh and ₹1.66 Cr OFS figures are 25,72,800 and 2,30,400 shares × ₹72, and they match chittorgarh.

The RHP is internally inconsistent: DSCR for FY25/FY24 is 2.45/2.50 on p130 but 0.13/0.06 on p134. Rice papad FY26 production is 1,02,031 kg on p130 but 10,20,031 kg on p134; the 93.15% utilisation matches 10,20,031.
The RHP's working-capital risk factor shows FY26 inventory as ₹2,416.62 lakh, but the restated balance sheet shows ₹2,498.61 lakh. The balance-sheet figure is used.
PAT growth of +10.33% understates the operating trend: PBT rose 53.46% because FY25 had zero current tax and FY26 had ₹178.61 lakh current tax plus ₹20.69 lakh earlier-year tax.
